question: In the method of moving average, the second average is the mean of the:

options.text: m terms from second to (m + 1)th term
m terms from fourth to (m + 3)th term
m terms from third to (m + 2)th term

solution:
The correct answer is 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the context of time series analysis or data smoothing, the method of moving averages involves calculating a sequence of averages by taking the mean of consecutive subsets of data. 
 
• In this method, the second average specifically refers to the mean of a specified number of terms, **starting from the second term and extending to the (m + 1)th term**, where 'm' represents the window size or a number of terms used for the moving average.
 
• Given a time series or sequence of data values X₁, X₂, X₃, X₄, X₅, X₆, X₇, ..., the method of moving average involves computing a series of averages to obtain smoothed values.
 
 
• The second average is determined by calculating the mean of a specific subset of terms, namely the terms from X₂ to the (m + 1)th term, where 'm' represents the chosen window size or the number of terms for the moving average.
 
• For instance, if the window size is set to 3, the second average is computed as the mean of the terms X₂, X₃, and X₄. If the window size is 5, the second average corresponds to the mean of the terms X₂, X₃, X₄, X₅, and X₆, and so on.
 
 
 
• The method of moving average is commonly employed for data smoothing purposes, enabling the identification of trends and patterns within a time series by reducing the impact of short-term fluctuations.

**Hence, in the method of moving average, the second average is the mean of the m terms from second to (m + 1)th term.**
